claim:
For the symmetric hyperbolic-sine jerk flow
\[
\dot x=y,\qquad \dot y=z,\qquad \dot z=-a x-b^2y-cz+d\sinh x,
\]
with \(b>0\), \(c>0\), and \(d>0\), a compact invariant set not contained in the origin exists if and only if \(a>d\). More precisely, when \(a\le d\), every bounded forward trajectory converges to \((0,0,0)\), every bounded complete trajectory is the constant origin trajectory, and the only compactly supported invariant probability measure is \(\delta_{(0,0,0)}\). When \(a>d\), there is a unique \(x_0>0\) satisfying \(\sinh(x_0)/x_0=a/d\), and \((\pm x_0,0,0)\) are nonzero equilibria, so nontrivial compact invariant sets exist. The proof is driven by the exact identity
\[
P=xz-\tfrac12y^2+cxy+\tfrac12b^2x^2,\qquad
\dot P=c y^2+(d-a)x^2+d\,x(\sinh x-x).
\]
For \(a\le d\) the right-hand side is nonnegative and vanishes only at \(x=y=0\). This establishes a sharp global compact-recurrence threshold at the same parameter surface \(a=d\) where the source identifies its local pitchfork bifurcation; it does not assert that all initial conditions are bounded.
integrity: The proof is analytic. A local symbolic script checks the displayed coboundary identity and equilibrium algebra; no finite numerical experiment is used as evidence for the infinite-time statements. The source's listed MSC classifications are all in root 34.
limitations: The result concerns bounded forward trajectories, bounded complete trajectories, compact invariant sets, and compactly supported invariant measures. It does not prove global boundedness of all solutions and does not classify dynamics for \(a>d\) beyond existence of nonzero equilibria. The literature comparison includes complete inspection of the introducing source and accessible material from the closest later jerk-system paper, but not that later paper's complete full text.
title: A sharp compact-recurrence threshold for a hyperbolic-sine jerk flow
